title: Sequence fingerprint anchor + shadow publish playbook for KV onboarding
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Goal: produce a repeatable, low-risk playbook to onboard a new model to KV-backed long-context serving that ties per-model sequence fingerprints to a pinned anchor version and publishes shadow-run performance profiles. This ticket defines the checks, artifacts, and automated steps for: 1) generating sequence fingerprints and session-length histograms, 2) selecting an anchor (version-pinned) runtime for a model cohort, 3) running shadow traffic with sampled prefixes to collect latency/cost/kv-hit heatmaps, and 4) automating profile publication with safelists and rollback triggers. The approach differs from existing flows by using a two-pass shadow run (fast exploratory + targeted tail pass), explicit session-boundary bucketing, and a lightweight sufficiency test that validates profile representativeness before pinning. Output artifacts: CSV sequence fingerprint catalog, per-model heatmap PNGs, a JSON profile bundle ready for the profile publisher, and a canonical playbook script that can be executed by SRE/Platform engineers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For any new model onboarded under this playbook we can produce a sequence fingerprint catalog and a profile bundle; 2) Published profile includes at least 95% of observed session-length mass for the sample corpus; 3) Shadow-run results identify candidate anchor version or provide fallback selection with clear metric deltas (latency P99, avg token cost, KV hit rate); 4) Automated publication job runs and posts a changelog entry in Confluence + creates a profile PR in GitHub; 5) Rollback triggers (latency/regression threshold) are defined and testable in the canary environment.
plan: Phase A: Instrumentation and data collection. Ship a short-run sampler that extracts sequence fingerprints and session boundary metadata from production traces (sampled, privacy-preserving). Phase B: Exploratory shadow runs. Execute 1M token exploratory shadow across candidate runtime builds to create heatmaps and basic latency/cost profiles. Phase C: Tail-focused shadow runs. Identify tail clusters from fingerprints and run targeted longer shadows to surface worst-case behaviors. Phase D: Profile generation and validation. Convert heatmaps + traces into profile bundles, run sufficiency checks against held-out samples, and mark candidate anchor. Phase E: Publish: push profile bundle to profile-service, create documentation and changelog, and schedule canary rollout with automatic monitoring.
rollout_steps: 1) Generate fingerprint catalog in a staging dataset. 2) Run exploratory shadow on staging runtime (48h). 3) Produce heatmaps and automatic cluster summaries. 4) Run tail shadows for clusters that contribute >5% of latency tail. 5) Validate profile sufficiency metrics; if pass, mark anchor version and create profile publish PR. 6) Deploy to canary with 2% traffic; monitor 24h for regressions. 7) If healthy, ramp to 20% then 100% per org policy. 8) If regressions detected, auto-roll back to previous anchor and open incident playbook.
metrics: Primary: P99 latency delta vs baseline, average tokens/sec, KV hit rate, per-token cost delta. Secondary: profile sufficiency coverage (percent mass covered by fingerprints), profile publication success rate, shadow-run sampling efficiency (tokens sampled per effective data point).
risks: - Sampling bias: small sample may not represent rare tail sessions. Mitigation: two-pass shadow with stratified tail sampling. - False anchors: choosing a version that performs worse on unseen workloads. Mitigation: sufficiency test and a conservative canary. - Privacy/regulatory exposure when sampling traces. Mitigation: remove PII, apply differential sampling thresholds and review with Security. - Operational cost of long shadow runs. Mitigation: cap token budget and use cost-aware routing.
